data.name: Rampyare
data.gender_notes: Rampyare is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Rampyare is a combination of two words, 'Ram' and 'Pyare'. Ram is the name of a popular Hindu deity, Lord Rama. Pyare means 'beloved' or 'dear'. Therefore, the name Rampyare signifies 'Lord Rama, the beloved one'. The name Rampyare carries the meaning “Lord Rama” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Rampyare usually hope their child will grow to embody lord rama and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Rampyare is believed to bring blessings of Lord Rama, who is known for his strength, power, and protection. It is a name that inspires devotion, love, and respect.
data.etymology: Rampyare belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Rama.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rampyare total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rampyare holds significant cultural relevance as it is a sacred name in Hinduism, derived from the name of the revered deity Lord Rama. Lord Rama, an ideal figure in Hindu culture, represents various virtues such as duty (Dharma), patience (Shanti), and morality (Satya). He is considered an embodiment of perfection and is respected and revered by millions of Hindus worldwide. Hence, the name Rampyare pays tribute to the cultural legacy of Lord Rama and instills a sense of reverence and attachment towards the deity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rampyare has deep spiritual significance, as it is a constant reminder of the presence and blessings of Lord Rama. Belief in the power and grace of deities is an essential aspect of Hindu spirituality. By bearing the name Rampyare, one connects spiritually with Lord Rama, seeking blessings and guidance in daily life. The name is a source of inner peace and strength, reassuring the bearer of the divine presence within, and reminding them of their spiritual potential. Additionally, the name inspires devotion and love towards Lord Rama and encourages the bearer to follow the path of truth, righteousness, and morality. It serves as a daily reminder of one's spiritual identity and values and motivates the individual to strive towards higher inner growth and Self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rampyare is a name rooted in valor and devotion. Rampya signifies one who holds the banner of Rama, symbolizing unwavering commitment to spiritual ideals and inner strength. Pyare means beloved, emphasizing the deep connection to the divine and the self.

historical_references.reference: Rampyare was a Jain monk and scholar during the 12th and 13th centuries in western India. He is best known for his works on the Jain text, the Agama, which provided commentaries and clarifications on the original texts.
historical_references.context: Jain monk and scholar in western India, worked on commentaries and clarifications of the Agama text.

historical_references.reference: Rampyare is also known to have played a significant role in the Jain community during the Alupa and Hoyasala kingdoms in Karnataka, India. He was the chief priest of the Jain temple at Shravanabelagola during the time of King Bira Ballala III and is credited with the construction of the massive statue of Bahubali that is a major tourist attraction today.
historical_references.context: Chief priest of Jain temple at Shravanabelagola during the Alupa and Hoyasala kingdoms, credited with the construction of a major statue of Bahubali.
